    15	 2531| \begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
    16	 2532|   Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
    17	 2533|   Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
    18	 2534|   Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
    19	 2535|   \[
    20	 2536|     J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},
    21	 2537|   \]
    22	 2538|   where each $K_{ij}$ is bounded on $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be
    23	 2539|   bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
    24	 2540|   and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
    25	 2541|   and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
    26	 2542|   every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
    27	 2543|   \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
    28	 2544|     \begin{split}
    29	 2545|       &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
    30	 2546|       (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
    31	 2547|       &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
    32	 2548|       J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
    33	 2549|     \end{split}
    34	 2550|   \end{equation}
    35	 2551|   The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
    36	 2552|   whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
    37	 2553| \end{lemma}
    38	 2554| 
    39	 2555| \begin{proof}
    40	 2556|   In normalized Hermite coordinates, multiplication by $g_{ij}$ maps
    41	 2557|   $h_{\boldsymbol a}$ to $\sqrt{a_{ij}+1}\,h_{\boldsymbol a+e_{ij}}
    42	 2558|   +\sqrt{a_{ij}}\,h_{\boldsymbol a-e_{ij}}$; the second term is zero if $a_{ij}
    43	 2559|   = 0$. Thus, it changes the total degree of color $i$ by one and leaves all
    44	 2560|   other color degrees unchanged. The operators $I\otimes F_l$ leave every
    45	 2561|   Gaussian degree unchanged. After the first $l$ insertions, the uncompressed
    46	 2562|   word therefore has color-$i$ degree at most $r_i(l) = |\{j\le l:i_j=i\}| \le
    47	 2563|   r_i \le N_i$. This is an induction starting from degree zero in every color.
    48	 2564|   Consequently, $P$ is the identity both before and after every insertion along
    49	 2565|   that word. Induction on $l$ now proves \eqref{E:finite-word-cutoff}. The
    50	 2566|   lowering term has been retained: the assertion includes creation followed by
    51	 2567|   annihilation and all resulting self-contractions. Linearity and equality of
    52	 2568|   the vector integrands prove the last assertion. This is an equality of
    53	 2569|   selected finite words, not of full propagators at a fixed cutoff. This proves
    54	 2570|   Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff}.
    55	 2571| \end{proof}

   165	 5171|   3/2$, it holds with
   166	 5172|   \[

   168	 5174|     \frac{2\alpha}{3/2-\alpha}4^{\alpha-3/2}\right\}.

   177	 5183|     {2\pi\sqrt{h^2-|y|^2}},\qquad
   178	 5184|     G_h^{(3)}(\ud y)=\frac{\sigma_h(\ud y)}{4\pi h},
   179	 5185|   \]

   181	 5187|   mass $h$ and satisfy $G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)$. Thus, the unsmoothed convolution is
   182	 5188|   $ch^{1-\alpha}F_d(z/h)$, where $F_d(w) = \int G_1^{(d)}(\ud
   183	 5189|   y)|y+w|^{-\alpha}$. In dimension three spherical coordinates give, for $\rho =
   184	 5190|   |w| > 0$,
   185	 5191|   \[
   186	 5192|     F_3(w)=\frac{(1+\rho)^v-|1-\rho|^v}{2v\rho},
   187	 5193|     \qquad v=2-\alpha\in(0,1).
   188	 5194|   \]
   189	 5195|   For $0 < \rho < 1$ this is the average of the convex function $f(s) =
   190	 5196|   (1+s)^{v-1}$ on $[-\rho,\rho]$. Its derivative has numerator
   191	 5197|   $\rho[f(\rho)+f(-\rho)]-\int_{-\rho}^\rho f(s)\ud s \ge 0$, by the endpoint
   192	 5198|   chord bound for a convex function. For $\rho > 1$, every distance
   193	 5199|   $\sqrt{1+\rho^2+2\rho u}$, $-1 \le u \le 1$, increases with $\rho$, so its
   194	 5200|   negative power decreases. The formula is continuous at $\rho = 1$ and at zero.

  1131	   62|     \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}=c^2/6.

  1138	   69|   is the exact premise and conclusion of the existing conditional WhiteCDF
  1139	   70|   square deduction. Here $A > 0$, since $A = 0$ would imply $f = 0$ a.e. Also $b
  1140	   71|   > 0$: zero derivative makes its continuous representative constant and hence
  1141	   72|   zero in $L^2$, contradicting unit mass. Thus, $A/\sqrt b \le 1/\sqrt3$.
  1142	   73| 
  1143	   74|   For $\ell > 0$ use the real smooth $H^1$ profile $f_\ell(x) =
  1144	   75|   \sqrt{\ell/2}\operatorname{sech}(\ell x)$, with $f_\ell' = -\ell\tanh(\ell
  1145	   76|   x)f_\ell$. Set $t = \tanh(\ell x)$, so $\ud t = \ell\operatorname{sech}^2(\ell
  1146	   77|   x)\ud x$. Direct integration gives
  1147	   78|   \[

   618	theorem terminal_wick_paper {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω)
   619	    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T)
   620	    (W : Pt d T → Ω → ℝ) (K : Pt d T → Pt d T → ℝ) (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P)
   621	    (hVfin : BddAbove (Set.range fun p => K p p))
   622	    (_hcell : MeanSquareCellContinuous K)
   623	    (ν : ∀ n : ℕ, Measure (Fin n → Pt d T)) [∀ n, IsFiniteMeasure (ν n)]
   624	    (hmass : ∀ n, ν n univ = chainMass d n T)
   625	    (hmeas : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW z) (ν n))
   626	    (hK : Measurable fun q : Pt d T × Pt d T => K q.1 q.2) :
   627	    (∀ n, Integrable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW z) (ν n)) ∧
   628	      ((chainIntegral ν hW 0 : Ω → ℝ) =ᵐ[P] fun _ => 1) ∧
   629	      (∀ n, ‖chainIntegral ν hW n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt ((2 * n - 1).doubleFactorial) *
   630	        (⨆ p, K p p) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * (T ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n).factorial)) ∧
   631	      (∀ m n, ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P =
   632	        ∑ D ∈ pairings (univ : Finset (Fin (m + n))), pairingIntegral ν K m n D) ∧
   633	      (∀ m n (D : Fin (m + n) → Fin (m + n)), Integrable (fun q : (Fin m → Pt d T) × (Fin n → Pt d T) =>
   634	        pairWeight (fun a b => K (Fin.append q.1 q.2 a) (Fin.append q.1 q.2 b)) univ D)
   635	        ((ν m).prod (ν n))) ∧
   636	      (∀ m n, Odd (m + n) → ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P = 0) ∧
   637	      ((∀ p q, 0 ≤ K p q) →
   638	        (∀ m n (D : Fin (m + n) → Fin (m + n)), 0 ≤ pairingIntegral ν K m n D) ∧
   639	        ∀ m n, 0 ≤ ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P) ∧
   640	      (∀ r : ℝ, Summable fun n => ‖r ^ n • chainIntegral ν hW n‖) ∧
   641	      ((∀ p q, 0 ≤ K p q) → ∀ r : ℝ,
   642	        UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput P (fun n => chainIntegral ν hW n) r) := by
   643	  set V := ⨆ p, K p p with hVdef
   644	  have hV : ∀ p, K p p ≤ V := fun p => le_ciSup hVfin p
   645	  have hV0 : 0 ≤ V := supVar_nonneg hW hT.le hVfin
   646	  have hmassR : ∀ n, (ν n).real univ = T ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n).factorial := by
   647	    intro n
   648	    rw [measureReal_def, hmass n, chainMass_eq d hd n T hT.le, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal]
   649	    positivity
   650	  refine ⟨integrable_prodL2 ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas, ?_, fun n => ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   651	  · refine chainIntegral_zero hW ν ?_
   652	    rw [hmass 0, chainMass_eq d hd 0 T hT.le]; simp
   653	  · have h := norm_chainIntegral_le ν hW V hV0 hV n
   654	    rwa [hmassR n, sqrt_pow_eq_rpow V hV0] at h
   655	  · exact fun m n => mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas hK m n
   656	  · exact fun m n D => integrable_pairWeight ν hK V (fun x y => hW.abs_le V hV x y) m n D
   657	  · exact fun m n h => mixed_moment_odd ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas m n h
   658	  · exact fun hpos => ⟨fun m n D => pairing_integral_nonneg ν hpos m n D,
   659	      fun m n => mixed_moment_nonneg ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas hpos m n⟩
   660	  · exact summable_norm_smul_chainIntegral ν hW V hV0 hV T hmassR
   661	  · exact fun hpos r => terminalWickInput_of_nonneg ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas T hmassR hpos r

   664	proof 3693-3695 at a284420), exact-hypothesis wrapper: two centered real
   665	Gaussian fields on `[0,T] × ℝ^d` with covariances `0 ≤ K₁ ≤ K₂` (entrywise),

   670	    (P₁ : Measure Ω₁) (P₂ : Measure Ω₂) [IsProbabilityMeasure P₁] [IsProbabilityMeasure P₂]
   671	    (d : ℕ) (_hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T)
   672	    (W₁ : Pt d T → Ω₁ → ℝ) (K₁ : Pt d T → Pt d T → ℝ) (hW₁ : CenteredGaussianField W₁ K₁ P₁)
   673	    (W₂ : Pt d T → Ω₂ → ℝ) (K₂ : Pt d T → Pt d T → ℝ) (hW₂ : CenteredGaussianField W₂ K₂ P₂)
   674	    (hV₁fin : BddAbove (Set.range fun p => K₁ p p))
   675	    (hV₂fin : BddAbove (Set.range fun p => K₂ p p))
   676	    (_hcell₁ : MeanSquareCellContinuous K₁) (_hcell₂ : MeanSquareCellContinuous K₂)
   677	    (ν : ∀ n : ℕ, Measure (Fin n → Pt d T)) [∀ n, IsFiniteMeasure (ν n)]
   678	    (_hmass : ∀ n, ν n univ = chainMass d n T)
   679	    (hmeas₁ : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW₁ z) (ν n))
   680	    (hmeas₂ : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW₂ z) (ν n))
   681	    (h0 : ∀ p q, 0 ≤ K₁ p q) (h12 : ∀ p q, K₁ p q ≤ K₂ p q) (m n : ℕ) :
   682	    ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW₁ m ω * chainIntegral ν hW₁ n ω ∂P₁ ≤
   683	      ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW₂ m ω * chainIntegral ν hW₂ n ω ∂P₂ :=
   684	  mixed_moment_mono ν hW₁ hW₂ _ _ (supVar_nonneg hW₁ hT.le hV₁fin) (supVar_nonneg hW₂ hT.le hV₂fin)
   685	    (fun p => le_ciSup hV₁fin p) (fun p => le_ciSup hV₂fin p) hmeas₁ hmeas₂ h0 h12 m n

     9	lines 188-206, the comparison sentence lines 201-205; proof lines 208-247, the

    11	
    12	Formalized (a standalone finite result supporting the label, not the label):
    13	* `gaussian_seminorm_moment_le` (and `gaussian_seminorm_moment_le_paper`): for
    14	  a finite index type `ι`, real `ι × ι` matrices `A`, `B` with `A` positive
    15	  semidefinite and `B - A` positive semidefinite (`A ≤ B` in the Loewner
    16	  order, TeX lines 240-241: `bᵀAb ≤ bᵀBb` for every real `b`), every seminorm `N`
    17	  on `ℝ^ι` (`EuclideanSpace ℝ ι`) and every real `p ≥ 1`, the functions
    18	  `x ↦ N(x)^p` are integrable against the centered Gaussian laws
    19	  `N(0,A)` and `N(0,B)` (`ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian`), and
    20	  `∫ N(x)^p dN(0,A) ≤ ∫ N(x)^p dN(0,B)` (TeX line 244:
    21	  `E‖X‖^p ≤ E‖X+Z‖^p`, with finiteness of both sides, lines 245-246).
    22	
    23	Outside this module (a D1 boundary, stated here and in the wrapper): the
    24	identification of `A` with the covariance matrix of the masked noise
    25	evaluations `W(ζ_R F_i)` and of `B` with the auxiliary Gram matrix of
    26	`N_R` (TeX lines 201-203 and 239-240), the noise identity
    27	`E:masked-actual-noise-norm`, the contraction extension and its joint
    28	Gaussianity (lines 199-201, 230-237).  None of these is formalized; the
    29	theorem below is the finite comparison those steps feed into.
    30	
    31	Supplied inputs: none.
    32	
    33	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: the moments are Bochner integrals, so both
    34	integrability statements are conclusions; `N` is an arbitrary seminorm (its
    35	continuity in finite dimension is proved, `seminorm_continuous`), which
    36	contains every norm of the TeX.

    38	Proof route.  As in the TeX (lines 241-246), with the coupling expressed by
    39	measures: `N(0,B) = N(0,A) ∗ N(0,B-A)` (`multivariateGaussian_conv`, by
    40	characteristic functions, `Measure.ext_of_charFun`) replaces "diagonalizing
    41	`B - A` constructs `Z` ... on a product space", and the integral against the
    42	convolution is the iterated integral over the product.  For fixed `x`,
    43	`y ↦ N(x+y)^p` is convex and `N(0,B-A)` is centered, so Jensen's inequality
    44	(`ConvexOn.map_integral_le`) gives `N(x)^p ≤ ∫ N(x+y)^p dN(0,B-A)(y)`; this is

    63	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (the coupling of TeX lines 242-244 as an

    65	`N(0,B) = N(0,A) ∗ N(0,B-A)`. -/
    66	theorem multivariateGaussian_conv {A B : Matrix ι ι ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef)
    67	    (hBA : (B - A).PosSemidef) :
    68	    multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) B =
    69	      (multivariateGaussian 0 A) ∗ (multivariateGaussian 0 (B - A)) := by
    70	  have hB : B.PosSemidef := by simpa using hA.add hBA
    71	  apply Measure.ext_of_charFun
    72	  funext x
    73	  rw [charFun_conv, charFun_multivariateGaussian hB, charFun_multivariateGaussian hA,
    74	    charFun_multivariateGaussian hBA]
    75	  rw [← Complex.exp_add]
    76	  congr 1
    77	  simp [Matrix.sub_mulVec]

    80	/-- Auxiliary: a seminorm on `ℝ^ι` is bounded by a multiple of the Euclidean norm,
    81	`N(x) ≤ (∑ᵢ N(eᵢ)) ‖x‖`. -/
    82	theorem seminorm_le_mul_norm (N : Seminorm ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι))
    83	    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) :
    84	    N x ≤ (∑ i, N (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) * ‖x‖ := by
    85	  have hx : x = ∑ i, x i • EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) := by
    86	    ext j
    87	    simp [Pi.single_apply]
    88	  calc N x = N (∑ i, x i • EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) := by rw [← hx]
    89	    _ ≤ ∑ i, N (x i • EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) := Finset.map_sum_le_sum N Finset.univ _
    90	    _ = ∑ i, ‖x i‖ * N (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) := by
    91	        simp only [map_smul_eq_mul]
    92	    _ ≤ ∑ i, ‖x‖ * N (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) :=
    93	        Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ =>
    94	          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (PiLp.norm_apply_le x i) (apply_nonneg N _)

   163	  have hconv := multivariateGaussian_conv hA hBA

  3600	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}
  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]
  3610	  These Bochner integrals exist in $L^2(\Omega)$ and satisfy
  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}
  3616	  For $m+n = 2k$, concatenate $\boldsymbol\tau =
  3617	  (s_1,\ldots,s_m,r_1,\ldots,r_n)$ and $\boldsymbol\eta =
  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then
  3619	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-wick-formula}
  3620	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),
  3622	  \end{equation}
  3623	  where, with both chains terminating at $(T,x)$,
  3624	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-pairing-integral}
  3625	    \begin{split}
  3626	      \mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}
  3627	      ={}&\int_{[0,T]^m_<\times[0,T]^n_<}
  3628	      \ud\boldsymbol s\,\ud\boldsymbol r
  3629	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\
  3630	      &\quad\times\prod_{j=1}^m
  3631	      G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j)
  3632	      \prod_{j=1}^n
  3633	      G_{r_{j+1}-r_j}(z_{j+1}-\ud z_j)\\
  3634	      &\quad\times\prod_{\{a,b\}\in D}
  3635	      \mathcal{K}(\tau_a,\eta_a;\tau_b,\eta_b).
  3636	    \end{split}
  3637	  \end{equation}
  3638	  Each pairing has coefficient one. If $m+n$ is odd, the expectation is zero.
  3639	  Empty chains and the case $m = n = 0$ have the usual empty-product meaning. If
  3640	  $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, every integral above is nonnegative. Consequently,
  3641	  entrywise comparison $0 \le \mathcal{K}_1 \le \mathcal{K}_2$ compares all
  3642	  finite partial-order second moments in the same direction. The series
  3643	  $\sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$ for every real or complex
  3644	  $r$.
  3645	\end{lemma}
  3646	
  3647	\begin{proof}
  3648	  The mass of $G_h$ is $h$. If $M_n(T)$ is the total mass of
  3649	  $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$, integration at the last vertex gives $M_0 = 1$ and
  3650	  $M_n(T) = \int_0^T(T-s)M_{n-1}(s)\ud s$. Induction therefore yields $M_n(T) =
  3651	  T^{2n}/(2n)!$. Gaussian moments and H\"older's inequality give
  3652	  \[
  3653	    \left\|\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\right\|_2
  3654	    \le\prod_{j=1}^n\|\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\|_{2n}
  3655	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}.
  3656	  \]
  3657	  Mean-square continuity of Gaussian variables implies their continuity in every
  3658	  fixed finite $L^p$. Hence, the product is strongly measurable in $L^2$ on the
  3659	  stated pieces. The finite kernel mass and the displayed bound prove Bochner
  3660	  integrability and~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}.
  3661	
  3662	  Fubini now passes expectation through the product of the two finite kernel
  3663	  measures. For the $m+n$ Gaussian variables at their labelled vertices,
  3664	  differentiate
  3665	  \[
  3666	    \E\exp\left(\sum_i t_i\mathcal{W}(\tau_i,\eta_i)\right)
  3667	    =\exp\left(\frac12\sum_{i,j}t_i t_j
  3668	    \mathcal{K}(\tau_i,\eta_i;\tau_j,\eta_j)\right)
  3669	  \]
  3670	  once in each $t_i$ at zero. Odd total degree gives zero. At degree $2k$ the
  3671	  result is the sum over unordered pair partitions, with one covariance product
  3672	  per pairing. Orientations and orderings of the $k$ pairs cancel the
  3673	  exponential's $2^k k!$ denominator. Integration
  3674	  gives~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula} with precisely the domains and
  3675	  coefficients in~\eqref{E:terminal-pairing-integral}.
  3676	
  3677	  Symmetrizing a chain measure does not change its stochastic integral: the
  3678	  product of its $n$ scalar field values is invariant under relabeling. Thus,
  3679	  averaging the $n!$ pushforwards of $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$ with coefficient
  3680	  $1/n!$ gives the same $Y_n$. There is no additional $n!$ factor
  3681	  in~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula}, or $m!n!$ in a two-chain product. This
  3682	  identifies the ordinary ordered regularized integrals and their symmetrized
  3683	  convention in~\eqref{E:expansion}.
  3684	
  3685	  In dimension three one may first replace $G$ by $p_\eta*G$. Those positive
  3686	  measures have the same masses and converge weakly to $G$. Off the finitely
  3687	  many time cut points, all finite Gaussian moments are bounded continuous
  3688	  functions of the spatial variables. Dominated convergence for their finite
  3689	  Wick sums proves the same limit for the mixed second moments with two Green
  3690	  widths. It gives $L^2$ convergence to the Bochner integral above, exactly the
  3691	  fixed-noise Green convention used in the source.
  3692	
  3693	  If $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, positivity of the Green measures makes each covariance
  3694	  product nonnegative. Comparing them proves the stated finite-moment
  3695	  monotonicity, including self-pairs and unequal chains. Finally, the ratio of
  3696	  successive right sides of~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}, with an additional
  3697	  factor $|r|^n$, is $|r|\sqrt V T^2/((2n+2)\sqrt{2n+1})$, which tends to zero.
  3698	  The zero-variance case is immediate. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick}.
  3699	\end{proof}

  5167	\begin{lemma}[Riesz spatial maxima]\label{L:higher-riesz}
  5168	  Let $\gamma(x) = c|x|^{-\alpha}$, $c > 0$. In dimension three, for $1 < \alpha
  5169	  < 2$, Hypothesis~\ref{H:spatial-maximum} holds with the optimal uniform
  5170	  constant $M_3 = c2^{1-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$. In dimension two, for $1 < \alpha <
  5171	  3/2$, it holds with
  5172	  \[
  5173	    M_2=c\left\{4^\alpha+
  5174	    \frac{2\alpha}{3/2-\alpha}4^{\alpha-3/2}\right\}.
  5175	  \]
  5176	\end{lemma}

  5179	  From Chen~\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(2.5), p.~7}, the wave
  5180	  measures are
  5181	  \[
  5182	    G_h^{(2)}(\ud y)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\{|y|<h\}}\ud y}
  5183	    {2\pi\sqrt{h^2-|y|^2}},\qquad
  5184	    G_h^{(3)}(\ud y)=\frac{\sigma_h(\ud y)}{4\pi h},
  5185	  \]
  5186	  where $\sigma_h$ is surface measure on the sphere of radius $h$. Both have
  5187	  mass $h$ and satisfy $G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)$. Thus, the unsmoothed convolution is
  5188	  $ch^{1-\alpha}F_d(z/h)$, where $F_d(w) = \int G_1^{(d)}(\ud
  5189	  y)|y+w|^{-\alpha}$. In dimension three spherical coordinates give, for $\rho =
  5190	  |w| > 0$,
  5191	  \[
  5192	    F_3(w)=\frac{(1+\rho)^v-|1-\rho|^v}{2v\rho},
  5193	    \qquad v=2-\alpha\in(0,1).
  5194	  \]
  5195	  For $0 < \rho < 1$ this is the average of the convex function $f(s) =
  5196	  (1+s)^{v-1}$ on $[-\rho,\rho]$. Its derivative has numerator
  5197	  $\rho[f(\rho)+f(-\rho)]-\int_{-\rho}^\rho f(s)\ud s \ge 0$, by the endpoint
  5198	  chord bound for a convex function. For $\rho > 1$, every distance
  5199	  $\sqrt{1+\rho^2+2\rho u}$, $-1 \le u \le 1$, increases with $\rho$, so its
  5200	  negative power decreases. The formula is continuous at $\rho = 1$ and at zero.
  5201	  Its maximum is therefore $F_3(e_1) = 2^{1-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$.

  5205	  where the density is at most $2/(\pi\sqrt7)$; its mass is at most
  5206	  $2R^2/\sqrt7$. If $A \ge 1/2$, write $y = (x,v)$. On the ball $|v| \le R$ and
  5207	  $x \ge 1/4$. Put $L = \sqrt{1-v^2}$. Inside the disk, $1-|y|^2 = (L-x)(L+x)$

  5209	  $(L-x)^{-1/2}$ gives at most $2\sqrt{2R}$. The $v$ range has length at most
  5210	  $2R$, giving mass at most $(2\sqrt2/\pi)R^{3/2} \le 2R^{3/2}$, as claimed.

   189	  The space $\mathcal{D}$ belongs to the original test-noise completion and
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}

   195	  \[
   196	    N_R(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   197	    \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
   198	  \]
   199	  Then $F \mapsto W(\zeta_RF)$ extends as a contraction from the null-quotient
   200	  completion for $N_R$ into the original $L^2(\Omega)$. The extension is
   201	  centered and jointly Gaussian. For finitely many real $F_1,\ldots,F_m \in
   202	  \mathcal{D}$, their masked covariance matrix is bounded in positive
   203	  semidefinite order by the matrix of auxiliary inner products. This gives
   204	  covariance comparison for every finite linear Gaussian image and every convex
   205	  norm power $p \ge 1$.

   207	
   208	\begin{proof}
   209	  For real spatial Schwartz $f,g$, put $h(z) = \int f(y+z)g(y)\ud y$. Fourier
   210	  inversion and Parseval give
   211	  \[
   212	    h(z) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}\widehat{f}(\xi)
   213	    \overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\ud\xi.
   214	  \]
   215	  Therefore,
   216	  \[
   217	    \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}h(z)\ud z
   218	    = (2\pi)^d\widehat{f}(-\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(-\xi)}.
   219	  \]
   220	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single test $h$ and reflect
   221	  $\xi$ using evenness of $\mu$. The spatial covariance is thus
   222	  $(2\pi)^d\int\widehat{f}(\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Summing
   223	  over the finitely many temporal factors gives
   224	  \eqref{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}. Schwartz decay, temperedness and temporal
   225	  integrability justify these pairings. If $W$ is initially given only on
   226	  compact spatial tests, smooth expanding cutoffs converge in the Schwartz
   227	  topology. The spectral form is continuous in that topology, admitting
   228	  $\mathcal{D}$ in the same completion.

   230	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}, applied with $H =
   231	  H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$, gives $\E W(\zeta_RF)^2 \le N_R(F)^2$. It annihilates
   232	  auxiliary-null tests. An auxiliary Cauchy sequence thus gives a Cauchy
   233	  sequence of noise evaluations in $L^2(\Omega)$, proving the contraction
   234	  extension and its uniqueness. Every finite linear combination of the limits is
   235	  an $L^2$ limit of centered Gaussian variables. Their variances converge, so
   236	  their characteristic functions prove that the limits remain jointly centered

    67	/-- The pairings (perfect matchings) of a finite set `S`, encoded as
    68	fixed-point-free involutions of `S`: maps `p : ι → ι` with `p x ∈ S`, `p x ≠ x`,
    69	`p (p x) = x` for `x ∈ S`, normalized by `p x = x` off `S` (so that each pairing
    70	of `S` is one function).  For `S` all of `Fin (2k)` these are the pair partitions
    71	`D ∈ Π_k` of the TeX (main TeX lines 3619-3622, 3670-3673). -/
    72	def pairings (S : Finset ι) : Finset (ι → ι) :=
    73	  univ.filter fun p => (∀ x ∈ S, p x ∈ S ∧ p x ≠ x ∧ p (p x) = x) ∧ ∀ x, x ∉ S → p x = x
    74	
    75	/-- The weight `∏_{{a,b} ∈ D} c(a,b)` of a pairing: one factor per pair, taken
    76	at its smaller element `a < p a` (so each unordered pair contributes exactly once,
    77	with coefficient one). -/
    78	def pairWeight (c : ι → ι → ℝ) (S : Finset ι) (p : ι → ι) : ℝ :=
    79	  ∏ x ∈ S with x < p x, c x (p x)
    80	
    81	/-- The pairing sum `Σ_{D} ∏_{{a,b} ∈ D} c(a,b)` over all pairings of `S`. -/
    82	def wickSum (c : ι → ι → ℝ) (S : Finset ι) : ℝ :=
    83	  ∑ p ∈ pairings S, pairWeight c S p
    84	
    85	/-- Membership in `pairings S`. -/
    86	theorem mem_pairings {S : Finset ι} {p : ι → ι} :
    87	    p ∈ pairings S ↔ (∀ x ∈ S, p x ∈ S ∧ p x ≠ x ∧ p (p x) = x) ∧ ∀ x, x ∉ S → p x = x := by
    88	  simp [pairings]
    89	
    90	/-- The empty set has exactly one pairing, the identity. -/
    91	theorem pairings_empty : pairings (∅ : Finset ι) = {id} := by
    92	  ext p
    93	  rw [mem_pairings, Finset.mem_singleton]
    94	  constructor
    95	  · rintro ⟨-, h⟩; funext x; exact h x (Finset.notMem_empty x)
    96	  · rintro rfl; exact ⟨fun x hx => absurd hx (Finset.notMem_empty x), fun x _ => rfl⟩
    97	
    98	/-- The empty pairing sum is `1` (empty product). -/
    99	theorem wickSum_empty (c : ι → ι → ℝ) : wickSum c ∅ = 1 := by
   100	  simp [wickSum, pairings_empty, pairWeight]
   241	theorem wickSum_eq_sum_erase (c : ι → ι → ℝ) (S : Finset ι) (a : ι) (ha : a ∈ S)
   242	    (hmin : ∀ x ∈ S, a ≤ x) :
   243	    wickSum c S = ∑ b ∈ S.erase a, c a b * wickSum c ((S.erase a).erase b) := by
   244	  have hmaps : ∀ p ∈ pairings S, p a ∈ S.erase a := by
   245	    intro p hp
   246	    rw [mem_pairings] at hp
   247	    obtain ⟨h1, h2, -⟩ := hp.1 a ha
   248	    exact Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨h2, h1⟩
   249	  rw [wickSum, ← Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps]
   250	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => fiber_sum c S a b ha hmin hb

   254	/-- Auxiliary: removing two distinct elements lowers the cardinality by two. -/
   255	theorem card_erase_erase {S : Finset ι} {a b : ι} (ha : a ∈ S) (hb : b ∈ S.erase a) :
   256	    ((S.erase a).erase b).card = S.card - 2 := by

   259	/-- A set of odd cardinality has no pairing: the pairing sum is `0`. -/
   260	theorem wickSum_odd (c : ι → ι → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
   261	    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.card = 2 * k + 1 → wickSum c S = 0 := by
   262	  induction k with
   263	  | zero =>
   264	    intro S hS
   265	    have hne : S.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.1 (by omega)
   266	    rw [wickSum_eq_sum_erase c S _ (S.min'_mem hne) (fun x hx => S.min'_le x hx)]
   267	    have : S.erase (S.min' hne) = ∅ := by
   268	      rw [← Finset.card_eq_zero, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (S.min'_mem hne)]; omega
   269	    simp [this]
   270	  | succ k ih =>
   271	    intro S hS
   272	    have hne : S.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.1 (by omega)
   273	    rw [wickSum_eq_sum_erase c S _ (S.min'_mem hne) (fun x hx => S.min'_le x hx)]
   274	    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun b hb => ?_
   275	    rw [ih _ (by rw [card_erase_erase (S.min'_mem hne) hb]; omega), mul_zero]
   276	
   277	/-- Auxiliary: with all weights `1`, the pairing sum counts the pairings. -/
   278	theorem wickSum_const_one (S : Finset ι) :
   279	    wickSum (fun _ _ => 1) S = (pairings S).card := by
   280	  simp [wickSum, pairWeight]
   281	
   282	/-- If `|c(a,b)| ≤ V` for all `a, b`, then the pairing sum over a set of `2k`
   283	elements is at most `(2k-1)!! V^k` in absolute value (there are `(2k-1)!!`
   284	pairings, each a product of `k` factors). -/
   285	theorem wickSum_abs_le (c : ι → ι → ℝ) (V : ℝ) (hc : ∀ x y, |c x y| ≤ V) (k : ℕ) :
   286	    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.card = 2 * k → |wickSum c S| ≤ ((2 * k - 1).doubleFactorial : ℝ) * V ^ k := by
   287	  induction k with
   288	  | zero =>
   289	    intro S hS
   290	    obtain rfl : S = ∅ := Finset.card_eq_zero.1 (by omega)
   291	    rw [wickSum_empty]; simp
   292	  | succ k ih =>
   293	    intro S hS
   294	    have hne : S.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.1 (by omega)
   295	    set a := S.min' hne
   296	    have ha : a ∈ S := S.min'_mem hne
   297	    have hV : 0 ≤ V := (abs_nonneg _).trans (hc a a)
   298	    rw [wickSum_eq_sum_erase c S a ha (fun x hx => S.min'_le x hx)]
   299	    refine (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans ?_
   300	    have hterm : ∀ b ∈ S.erase a, |c a b * wickSum c ((S.erase a).erase b)| ≤
   301	        V * (((2 * k - 1).doubleFactorial : ℝ) * V ^ k) := by
   302	      intro b hb
   303	      rw [abs_mul]
   304	      exact mul_le_mul (hc a b) (ih _ (by rw [card_erase_erase ha hb]; omega))
   305	        (abs_nonneg _) hV
   306	    refine (Finset.sum_le_sum hterm).trans ?_
   307	    rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_erase_of_mem ha, hS, nsmul_eq_mul]
   308	    have hdf : (2 * (k + 1) - 1).doubleFactorial = (2 * k + 1) * (2 * k - 1).doubleFactorial := by
   309	      rcases k with _ | k
   310	      · simp
   311	      · rw [show 2 * (k + 1 + 1) - 1 = (2 * k + 1) + 2 by omega, Nat.doubleFactorial_add_two,
   312	          show 2 * (k + 1) - 1 = 2 * k + 1 by omega]; ring
   313	    rw [hdf, show 2 * (k + 1) - 1 = 2 * k + 1 by omega]
   314	    push_cast
   315	    ring_nf
   316	    exact le_rfl

   318	/-- A set of `2k` elements has `(2k-1)!!` pairings (`Nat.doubleFactorial`; `(-1)!! = 0!! = 1`). -/
   319	theorem card_pairings_even (k : ℕ) (S : Finset ι) (hS : S.card = 2 * k) :
   320	    (pairings S).card = (2 * k - 1).doubleFactorial := by
   321	  have h : ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ S : Finset ι, S.card = 2 * k →
   322	      wickSum (fun _ _ => 1) S = ((2 * k - 1).doubleFactorial : ℝ) := by
   323	    intro k
   324	    induction k with
   325	    | zero =>
   326	      intro S hS
   327	      obtain rfl : S = ∅ := Finset.card_eq_zero.1 (by omega)
   328	      rw [wickSum_empty]; simp
   329	    | succ k ih =>
   330	      intro S hS
   331	      have hne : S.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.1 (by omega)
   332	      have ha : S.min' hne ∈ S := S.min'_mem hne
   333	      rw [wickSum_eq_sum_erase _ S _ ha (fun x hx => S.min'_le x hx)]
   334	      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => by
   335	        rw [ih _ (by rw [card_erase_erase ha hb]; omega), one_mul]]
   336	      rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_erase_of_mem ha, hS, nsmul_eq_mul]
   337	      have hdf : (2 * (k + 1) - 1).doubleFactorial = (2 * k + 1) * (2 * k - 1).doubleFactorial := by
   338	        rcases k with _ | k
   339	        · simp
   340	        · rw [show 2 * (k + 1 + 1) - 1 = (2 * k + 1) + 2 by omega, Nat.doubleFactorial_add_two,
   341	            show 2 * (k + 1) - 1 = 2 * k + 1 by omega]; ring
   342	      rw [hdf, show 2 * (k + 1) - 1 = 2 * k + 1 by omega]
   343	      push_cast; ring
   344	  have := h k S hS
   345	  rw [wickSum_const_one] at this
   346	  exact_mod_cast this

   348	/-- A set of odd cardinality has no pairings. -/
   349	theorem card_pairings_odd (k : ℕ) (S : Finset ι) (hS : S.card = 2 * k + 1) :

   355	/-- Nonnegative weights give a nonnegative pairing sum. -/
   356	theorem wickSum_nonneg (c : ι → ι → ℝ) (hc : ∀ x y, 0 ≤ c x y) (S : Finset ι) :
   357	    0 ≤ wickSum c S :=

   362	    (S : Finset ι) : wickSum c₁ S ≤ wickSum c₂ S :=
   363	  Finset.sum_le_sum fun p _ =>
   364	    Finset.prod_le_prod₀ (fun x _ => h0 x (p x)) fun x _ => h12 x (p x)
